card.flavorText: The 24th Ulan Regiment of the Grand Chancellor of the Crown Stanisław Żółkiewski was a cavalry unit of the Polish Army that fought during WWII, particularly in the Invasion of Poland in September 1939. Formed as part of Poland’s traditional uhlan (light cavalry) forces, the regiment belonged to the 10th Motorized Cavalry Brigade, which was one of the first Polish units to be fully motorized. During the German invasion, the 24th Uhlan Regiment fought in several key battles, using a mix of cavalry and mechanized tactics to delay the advancing German Wehrmacht. The regiment fought in the Battles of Jordanów and Wysoka, as well as in Łańcut, Rzeszów, and Radymno. On September 19th, 1939, it crossed into Hungary, avoiding capture by German or Soviet forces. In recognition of its soldiers' bravery, the unit was awarded the Virtuti Militari. In 1940, the regiment was reformed in France and later in England. From 1943 the regiment fought in Western Europe as part of the 10th Armoured Cavalry Brigade.
